messages.author: 5ce1f1f0b0b32cf2
messages.subject: Adjusting for Covariates in a Cross-Lagged Panel Model
parts:
Hello all, 

I was wondering if someone could advise on how to adjust a CLPM for simple covariates such as age and sex. 

My CLPM takes this form: 

cl_ld_1 <-
  '
#Regressions
FREQ_DEP_1 ~ FREQ_DEP_0 + OUTDOOR_SUMMER_0
OUTDOOR_SUMMER_1 ~ FREQ_DEP_0 + OUTDOOR_SUMMER_0

#Covariances
FREQ_DEP_0 ~~ OUTDOOR_SUMMER_0
FREQ_DEP_1~~ OUTDOOR_SUMMER_1
'
fit_cl_ld_1 <- sem(cl_ld_1, data=d1, ordered=(' FREQ_DEP_1  '), estimator='PML', std.lv = TRUE, verbose = TRUE)
summary(fit_cl_ld_1, fit.measures=T, standardized=T, rsquare=T)

To add in adjustment for age and sex, I was planning on adding covariances for age and sex with each of the variables at each time point. E.g. by doing the following: 

cl_ld_2 <-
  '
#Regressions
FREQ_DEP_1~ FREQ_DEP_0 + OUTDOOR_SUMMER_0
OUTDOOR_SUMMER_1 ~ FREQ_DEP_0 + OUTDOOR_SUMMER_0

#Covariances
FREQ_DEP_0 ~~ OUTDOOR_SUMMER_0
FREQ_DEP_1~~ OUTDOOR_SUMMER_1
AGE ~~ OUTDOOR_SUMMER_0
AGE ~~ FREQ_DEP_0
SEX ~~ OUTDOOR_SUMMER_0
SEX ~~ FREQ_DEP_0
AGE ~~ OUTDOOR_SUMMER_1
AGE ~~ FREQ_DEP_1
SEX ~~ OUTDOOR_SUMMER_1
SEX ~~ FREQ_DEP_1'

fit_cl_ld_2 <- sem(cl_ld_2, data=d1, ordered=('FREQ_DEP_1'), estimator='PML', std.lv = TRUE, verbose = TRUE, em.iter.max = 100)
summary(fit_cl_ld_2, fit.measures=T, standardized=T, rsquare=T)

Does that sound about right? or would a better approach be using regression equations?

Kind regards and much appreciation for any insights you can offer. 

Angus

messages.author: 12fdd832cacb825e
messages.subject: Re: Adjusting for Covariates in a Cross-Lagged Panel Model
parts:
Regressions are the standard approach for covariates/ confounds in SEM. That's more analogous to simultaneous multiple regression. 

I don't think adding covariances will tell you much.

Sure! Here it is: 

cl_ld_2 <-
  '
#Regressions
FREQ_DEP_0 ~ AGE + SEX
OUTDOOR_SUMMER_0 ~ AGE + SEX
FREQ_DEP_1 ~ FREQ_DEP_0 + OUTDOOR_SUMMER_0 + AGE + SEX
OUTDOOR_SUMMER_1 ~ FREQ_DEP_0 + OUTDOOR_SUMMER_0 + AGE + SEX

#Covariances
FREQ_DEP_0 ~~ OUTDOOR_SUMMER_0
FREQ_DEP_1 ~~ OUTDOOR_SUMMER_1
'
fit_cl_ld_2 <- sem(cl_ld_2, data=d1, ordered=c('FREQ_DEP_0',' FREQ_DEP_1'), estimator='PML', std.lv = TRUE, verbose = TRUE)
summary(fit_cl_ld_2, fit.measures=T, standardized=T, rsquare=T, ci=T)

I ran this model again and it doesn't seem to be converging now - though I thought it worked before. I get the following error which appears to be due to the PML estimator: 

" Error in pml_deriv1(Sigma.hat = Sigma.hat[[g]], Mu.hat = Mu.hat[[g]],  :
  lavaan ERROR: mixed + exo in PML not implemented; try optim.gradient = "numerical" " 

Regards,
Angus
